title: Dispatch: 91o0 PR #613 review fixes - per-instance coverage + same-level Lore expertise (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Fix dispatch for PR #613 review (GitHub review 5464545677, head 4ba97273), eshyra-91o0. Model: Sonnet 5.5 (Claude Agent). Worktree .worktrees/eshyra-91o0.2 on branch eshyra-91o0.2, cut from eshyra-91o0 @ 4ba97273 (already contains merged PR #612 expertise). Run `npm ci` first. Read the review: `gh api repos/jbongaarts/eshyra/pulls/613/reviews --jq '.[].body'`. Two blocking findings. Fix both in this one round, along with their siblings.

FINDING 1 — coverage invariant is per-feature, must be per-choice-instance.
packages/core/src/character/levelUpChoiceCoverage.ts builds `covered` from descriptor featureRefs and skips a whole feature once any descriptor names it. So a feature with one handled choice and one unhandled choice lets the unhandled one through. The base Spellcasting/Pact Magic exemption ("some level.N.spells.* descriptor exists") is the same mistake.

DESIGN (supervisor decision):
- Introduce an explicit HANDLED-INSTANCE contract. Every detector reports the choice instances it took responsibility for at this level as keys `${featureRef}\0${choiceId}`, INCLUDING instances it evaluated and decided need no descriptor. Examples: a replacement with nothing held; a conditional spell choice whose trigger was not picked; a non-due spell choice on a held feature. Put a small shared type/helper (e.g. `choiceInstanceKey(featureRef, choiceId)`) in levelUpChoiceCoverage.ts.
- Who handles what:
  * levelUpFeatureChoices.detectFeatureChoiceDescriptors: every list choice it processed (new, grown, repeated, replacement). Do NOT mark the CONDITIONAL_CHOICES ids handled here; the spell module owns them. Keep coveredFeatureRefs only for dropping the legacy fallback.
  * levelUpSpells.detectSpellDescriptors: (a) on non-base features, every spell/cantrip choice it evaluated in dueFeatureSpellChoices's scan (due or not, including conditional ones); (b) on the base Spellcasting/Pact Magic feature, when it is a target ref, map the bucket logic to the base choice ids it actually evaluates: cantrips->'cantrips', known->'spells', replacement->'spell-replacement', spellbook growth->'spellbook-growth', prepare->'prepared-spells'. Mark one handled only when the corresponding branch ran, i.e. `casts && toSpellcasting !== undefined` and the class preparation kind selects that branch. 'spellbook-initial' is creation-only. Do not mark it; if it is ever a level-up target instance, the invariant must block. When the legacy-classification failure returns early, its unsupported descriptor already blocks (see the next rule). Return handled instances alongside the descriptors (change the return shape, or add a sibling function; your choice, but keep one source of truth).
  * levelUpExpertise / levelUpSkillChoices: the choices they process. A repeated Lore grant is NOT handled by the skill module, so the invariant blocks it.
  * Legacy featureRequiredChoice in levelUpEngine.ts: a SUPPORTED 'subclass' descriptor handles the feature's 'subclass'-category choices. A SUPPORTED 'ability-score-improvement' descriptor handles the feature's 'asiOrFeat'-category choices (both 'ability-score-improvement' and the 'feat' marker: that descriptor's `from` already offers feats and resolution applies featRef; verify this before relying on it).
  * Blocking rule: an UNSUPPORTED descriptor carrying featureRef X blocks the level-up, so every instance on X counts as covered. Only that rule may cover by featureRef.
- The invariant then emits an unsupported descriptor for each instance at toLevel (keep choiceInstancesAtLevel semantics) that is neither handled nor covered by an unsupported descriptor on its feature, minus isUseTimeChoice. DELETE isBaseSpellcastingRef and the spellModuleEmitted shortcut.
- Re-run the class x subclass x level 1->20 enumeration (the existing test at levelUpSubclassChoices.test.ts ~434). Every transition must still report no uncovered instance. If one now appears, it is a real gap: fix the owning detector's handled set honestly, or report it. Never re-add a blanket exemption. Ranger/paladin 1->2 are the known sensitive cases (spell-replacement with nothing held -> the replacement branch evaluated it -> handled).

FINDING 2 — at bard 2->3, College of Lore's new skills must be eligible for Expertise in the same level-up.
detectExpertiseDescriptors reads only sheet.skillProficiencies (level 2), so a skill picked for Lore in this step is excluded and refused.
DESIGN: in detectLevelUpRequiredChoices, run detectSkillChoiceDescriptors BEFORE detectExpertiseDescriptors. For each supported skill descriptor that has a selection in `selections`, validate it with resolveSkillChoiceSelection (the same validation apply uses). Only on ok, collect its skillProficiencies as pending. Pass the pending skills to detectExpertiseDescriptors, e.g. as `pendingSkillProficiencies`, so eligibleOptions treats them as held. Invalid Lore picks contribute nothing, and the Lore descriptor still blocks on its own. applyLevelUp/preview already pass input.choices to detection, so resolution validates expertise against the expanded `from`. Persistence stays atomic: nothing is written while any blocker remains. The descriptor order (expertise before featureChoices) may change; that's fine. Check whether any other same-level interaction feeds expertise or skill eligibility (e.g. a background/feat grant at level-up). Report it if found; don't build speculative plumbing.

EVIDENCE (proportionate, generalized; extend levelUpSubclassChoices.test.ts):
- F1: one generalized test on a feature carrying BOTH a handled list choice and an unhandled choice (synthetic resolver/pack overlay, as the existing synthetic test does). The unhandled one must yield an unsupported descriptor and apply must refuse. Also cover a conditional sibling (e.g. a Pact-of-the-Tome-style requiresFeatureOption choice not triggered) to show it is not wrongly required, and a repeated grant.
- F2: a real bard 2->3 College of Lore regression using the REAL pack row (do not strip expertise; remove the existing test's expertise-stripping workaround, since expertise is now supported). Pick 3 Lore skills, including one not previously held, then Expertise on that new skill plus another: apply succeeds, and the sheet gets the skills and both featureChoices entries. Also: Expertise on a skill only in an INVALID Lore selection (held/duplicate) blocks; a duplicate Expertise pick blocks.
- `npm run verify:worktree` before committing.
notes:
Dispatched 2026-10-09 to Sonnet 5.5 Claude Agent (background), worktree .worktrees/eshyra-91o0.2 @4ba97273.
Completed @ffc2d6db (verify:worktree 6080 pass / 3 skip). F1: levelUpChoiceCoverage.ts now compares per instance via choiceInstanceKey(featureRef, choiceId) and a handled-instance set; isBaseSpellcastingRef and the spellModuleEmitted shortcut deleted. Only an UNSUPPORTED descriptor with featureRef covers by ref. descriptorId/featureSlug moved to coverage module (re-exported from levelUpFeatureChoices) to avoid an import cycle. Handled ownership: featureChoices = every list choice processed (new/grown/repeated/replacement, incl. held invocation choices); conditional ids NOT marked (spell module owns). Spells = non-base spell/cantrip choices evaluated in dueFeatureSpellChoices (due, untriggered conditional, or non-due on held/repeated feature) + base Spellcasting/Pact Magic: cantrips (casts&&toSpellcasting), spells+spell-replacement (kind known), spellbook-growth (spellbookStartingSpells), prepared-spells (kind prepared); spellbook-initial never marked; legacy-classification early return marks nothing. Expertise = expertise-category choices on target refs. Skills = skill list choices on first-grant refs (repeated Lore grant unhandled -> invariant blocks). Engine legacy: supported subclass descriptor handles 'subclass' category; supported ASI descriptor handles 'asiOrFeat' (both ability-score-improvement and feat; verified from offers feats and resolution sets featRef). detectSpellDescriptors/Skill/Expertise/FeatureChoices now return handledInstances. Enumeration: existing class x subclass x 1->20 test passes with no uncovered instance, so no real gaps surfaced (ranger/paladin 1->2 fine). Deviation: in the spell scan a FIRST grant of a non-conditional, non-due spell choice is deliberately left unhandled so the invariant blocks it (not a principled skip). F2: engine runs detectSkillChoiceDescriptors first, validates each selected skill descriptor with resolveSkillChoiceSelection, passes valid skills as pendingSkillProficiencies to detectExpertiseDescriptors (eligibleOptions treats them as held, case-insensitive dedupe); invalid Lore picks add nothing. Descriptor order is now expertise, featureChoices, skills. Other same-level interactions: none found (level-up feats grant no skills). Tests (levelUpSubclassChoices.test.ts): Lore tests now use the real bard row (expertise-stripping removed); real bard 2->3 apply with Expertise on new Lore skill + held skill; invalid/duplicate Lore selection and duplicate Expertise block; F1 synthetic tests: handled+unhandled on one feature (unsupported + preview refuses), untriggered conditional spell sibling not required, repeated Lore grant blocked.
